raw_case_text:
A 46-year-old female from Hulunbeir City, Inner Mongolia, presented with a two-month history of intermittent high fever (up to 40.1 C) accompanied by persistent neck, shoulder, and back pain. Despite having no direct contact with cattle, sheep, dogs, or consumption of raw meat and dairy products, her symptoms persisted. She reported a weight loss of 2.5 kg, normal bowel habits, and poor sleep due to pain, without any signs of fatigue or night sweats. Upon her initial consultation at our hospital Orthopedics Outpatient Department on June 1, 2021, she was admitted for suspected cervical brucellosis spondylitis. Physical examination revealed significant tenderness at the C7 spinous process and paravertebral areas, limited cervical spine mobility, and radiating pain to the right upper limb. Neurological examination showed reduced right triceps tendon reflex and a muscle strength of grade 3 in the right upper limb. Diagnostic tests were performed to clarify her condition. The Rose Bengal plate agglutination test was positive, suggesting brucellosis. Concurrently, tuberculosis screening via T-SPOT showed increased spots of interferon alpha and beta, and a positive PPD test, though tuberculosis antibodies were negative, and no acid-fast bacilli were detected in sputum smears. Initial investigations showed leukopenia (WBC 4.57x109/L) with relative neutrophilia (51.3%), and anemia with a hemoglobin level of 103 g/L. Inflammatory markers were mildly elevated (CRP 0.5 mg/L, ESR 7mm/hr). Imaging studies, including X-rays, CT, and MRI scans of the cervical spine, demonstrated destructive spondylitis at the C7 vertebral level with paravertebral abscess formation (Figure 1). Based on these findings, a diagnosis of Brucella cervical spondylitis was confirmed.
Treatment began with a two-week regimen of antibiotics, including doxycycline, rifampin, levofloxacin, and ceftazidime-sulbactam. Surgical intervention was deemed necessary due to the persistence of symptoms and imaging findings. The patient underwent anterior cervical debridement and decompression, C7 subtotal corpectomy, and titanium mesh bone graft fusion, with a cervical titanium plate for internal fixation (Figure 2). The surgery involved meticulous removal of the infected tissue and decompression of the cervical spine. Postoperative care included continued antibiotic therapy, nourishment for nerve recovery, and precautions to prevent esophageal and respiratory complications. Pathology from intraoperative samples confirmed extensive Brucella involvement via Gram staining and RT-PCR, while tuberculosis was excluded (Figure 3). Follow-up at six months showed significant improvement in pain, recovery of muscle strength to grade 5 in the right upper limb (Figure 4), and normalization of inflammatory markers.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old female presented with a 2-month history of intermittent high fever and persistent neck, shoulder, and back pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced intermittent high fevers peaking up to 40.1 °C accompanied by persistent neck, shoulder, and back pain for 2 months. She reported poor sleep due to pain and a weight loss of 2.5 kg since symptom onset. Bowel habits were normal, and she denied fatigue or night sweats.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of Hulunbeir City, Inner Mongolia. Denied direct contact with cattle, sheep, or dogs, and denied consumption of raw meat or unpasteurized dairy products. No prior medical illnesses or chronic conditions reported.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports poor sleep due to pain and weight loss of 2.5 kg. Denies fatigue, night sweats, or changes in bowel habits.

objective.physical_examination: Significant tenderness at the C7 spinous process and paravertebral areas; limited cervical spine mobility; radiating pain to the right upper limb. Neurological examination: diminished right triceps tendon reflex; muscle strength of grade 3/5 in the right upper limb.
objective.routine_investigations: White blood cell count (WBC): 4.57 x 10^9/L (neutrophils 51.3%), hemoglobin: 103 g/L, C-reactive protein (CRP): 0.5 mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR): 7 mm/hr. Plain cervical X-ray showed destructive changes at C7.
objective.advanced_workup: CT and MRI scans of the cervical spine demonstrated destructive spondylitis at the C7 vertebral level with paravertebral abscess formation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Rose Bengal plate agglutination test was positive; intraoperative pathology confirmed extensive Brucella involvement by Gram staining and reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), confirming Brucella cervical spondylitis with paravertebral abscess. Differential diagnosis: Tuberculosis investigated and excluded; T-SPOT showed increased spots of interferon alpha and beta, and PPD was positive, but serum tuberculosis antibodies were negative and sputum smears showed no acid-fast bacilli. Management and Outcome: Preoperatively received a 2-week course of doxycycline, rifampin, levofloxacin, and ceftazidime-sulbactam. Underwent anterior cervical debridement and decompression, C7 subtotal corpectomy, titanium mesh bone graft fusion, and anterior cervical titanium plate fixation. Postoperatively, antibiotic therapy and nerve nourishment were continued. At 6-month follow-up, she demonstrated significant pain relief, recovery of right upper limb strength to grade 5/5, and normalization of inflammatory markers.
